notes: Nell Gannet (bible 5.13), keeper of the Drowned Gull and queen of the Low Tide Company. Voice: gold-toothed, delighted, 'darling'; everything's for sale. THIEF COMMISSION DROP (bible 4.3, the thief commission): a thief holding the horn-coin (commission.coin-held, stand-in until the item exists) meets her first at the entry 'commission' and chooses deliver, keep or a fake; each sets commission.outcome and emits commission.dropped for the world consequences (follow-up bead). SECRETS: bay nine (only to a thief or at disposition >= 10, nell.bay-nine-told), the relic-skimming and her go-between role (disposition >= 8, nell.skimming-confessed), the Undertow (opened for a thief by her class deal, or at disposition >= 6). Class deals: knight (warning), archer (Gull Shoot sponsor), sorcerer (restricted books past customs), thief (Undertow access). Stock and prices are out of scope (E20, E21); jobs and quests are hooks. mw-e39.22: ask-book (her betting book on the Tidefair; starts the Tidefair quest) and ask-strongroom (the roof hatch, for Contraband Pages).

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Well, well. A quiet one, with quiet hands. And that bulge in your pocket isn't your lunch, is it, darling? Let's have a look, then, nice and slow.

options.text: I'm keeping it. Tell your buyer I was never here.
Here you are. One horn-coin. Entirely genuine.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Lovely. Pleasure doing business, and a thirty-coin pleasure it is. Mr. S— will be delighted, and I'll be delighted on commission. Drinks on the house, thief to thief.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Keep it? Keep it! Oh, darling, you'll be wanting a new city, then. I'll tell him you never came. I'm very good at not seeing people. Don't make me practise.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Hm. It's a lovely piece. Warm in the hand, honest in the weight. You're either very good or very stupid, and I've known a lot of both. I'll pass it on, and we'll all find out together.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Break anything, you buy it, and then you own it, and then you'll have to sell it to me. Welcome to the Drowned Gull, darling. Nell Gannet. Sit, drink, don't swing that.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: A bow in the Gull! Lovely. Don't loose it indoors, but there's a gull shoot at the Tidefair and I'm always looking for someone who can hit the thing. Sit, darling.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Oh, you've a smell about you, darling. Ink, and ozone, and bad decisions. That's good. I sell restricted books, and I'll tell you how to get them past customs. For a little more.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Well. Hello, kin. You walk like you're not walking. Come in, sit, and I'll pour you something that isn't poison. Not yet.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Everything in Wendmouth's for sale, darling. Some of it's even ours. Nell Gannet, the Drowned Gull. What'll it be?

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Back again! The Gull's open, my pockets are not. What'll it be?

options.text: Any work for the Low Tide Company?
I hear your cellar goes further than your cellar.
Is it true you skim a coin from every relic crate?
I'll shoot for you at the Tidefair.
I'm looking for the way down.
I hear you keep a book on the Tidefair.
What do you know about Cray's strongroom?

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Mind how you go, darling. Mind the steps, mind the tide, mind your pockets. Not that you will.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Two coins, and the best thing you'll taste all day. Not that that's saying much. Cheers, darling.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Two coins, darling, not two sighs. The Gull's generous but she's not an idiot.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Vane crates go into bay nine and customs never cracks a seal. Funny, that. And the Inspector reads every book she confiscates, every single one. Even the ones with kissing. You didn't hear it from me.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Seals nobody cracks, darling. That's all a smuggler needs to know. And, between us, all a smuggler wants to ask.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Every one. She carries them home in a sack and brings back the empty sack. I'd be charmed, if she weren't trying to ruin me.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: For you, darling? Always. There's a warehouse and a crate and a chap with a veil, and they all want visiting. Come back when you've seen the dock at night.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Work for the Company? You've an honest face, which is a terrible handicap. I'll find you something small. Ask the dock, ask Big Oona, ask the tide.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: My cellar goes down to the bilges, darling, and no further. Whoever told you different is selling something. Probably me.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: It goes further. It goes under the wharf, under the breakwater, and out to the sea-door where the cargo doesn't need a stamp. The Undertow, we call it. Don't call it anything else.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Bay nine? A very large cupboard, darling, with a very large lock. Ask me again when I like you better.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Horn-coins, carvings, and a stone with a name on it. Forty of the first, three of the second. Vane's. And due on the Gilded Tern before the week's out, so don't wait too long.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Skim? From the relics? Darling, I'm a respectable innkeeper. A coin from every crate is a tax, and I'm a very fair taxman.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: One coin per crate, and not a coin more. A fee for being the middle of it all. I'm the go-between for Mr. S—'s agent, and it's a thankless trade. Don't repeat it.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Bless your heart. You break it, you buy it, you own it, and then you sell it to me. That's how the Gull works. Smash with confidence.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: The Gull Shoot! I'll sponsor you, darling, for a cut. Wooden gulls on a swinging boom, then a live one that nicked the prize ribbon. You'll hate it. I'll make a fortune.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Restricted, lovely. I've shelves of it under the stairs. Pay me, and I'll tell you how to carry it past Cray. Pay me more, and I'll tell you where she keeps her own.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: The way down. Kin, you're in. Second step, loose board, and a knock I'll teach you. Don't tell the Inspector. Don't tell the Gull. Don't tell the tide.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: The Book! Odds on every event, darling, and on every loser. Back yourself, or, if you mean to fall over, fall over with me: I pay for a graceful tumble at the table, the boom, wherever. Don't tell Oona. I'll deny it. Beautifully.

nodes.speaker: nell
nodes.text: Cray's strongroom? Iron door, a grille no one fits through, and a roof hatch she's reported to the Court as a skylight so she'll never be asked to fix it. A friend of mine would want the net lofts and a head for heights. Only a friend.
